segments.t: You had a chance to invest with Jeff Bezos very early
and you didn't.
Why?
I'm so stupid.
Don't embarrass me.
I'm so much regretting my life.
He and I were just one-on-one in a small, small hotel
in Switzerland, talking a couple of hours, investing.
And he and I almost agreed.
And, you know.
What year was this?
Before his IPO, before his IPO.
So, we were talking, you know,
Softbank invest a hundred million dollars
to own 30% of his company.
And so the variation we were talking was like $300 million.
And he said, no, Massa, you're crazy.
We're not 300 million company.
He's a, we are 350 million company.
So, the gap was only $50 million.
And we were talking.
And I said, okay, okay, maybe you're right.
Maybe we are close enough.
And I would talk to my guys in Tokyo and come back to you.
And right after the trip, I went to talk to my guys
and everybody said, maybe that's crazy idea.
Maybe you're right, but where is money?
And after discussing one hour, I said, well, you're right.
We don't have money.
So, we gave up that idea.
Well, let me ask you about one thing
that's been in the news over the past year
and you've called it a mistake.
And so I'm curious what the lesson is for you.
We work, of course, was something you've talked about
being a mistake.
Now that you've thought about it
and spent some time trying to learn from it,
what was the lesson?
